items.question: Fix a real point a and a natural number k, and prescribe target values v(0), v(1), ..., v(k). Define a degree-at-most-k real polynomial P by taking the local Taylor polynomial centred at a whose coefficient of (x-a)^j is v(j)/j!. Prove that for every j with 0 <= j <= k the ordinary j-th derivative of P evaluated at a equals exactly v(j). You may use the fact that the j-th derivative of a polynomial at a point equals j! times the degree-j Taylor coefficient of the polynomial about that point.

items.question: A block encoding is read by preparing the auxiliary register in the all-zero state, applying U, and postselecting the auxiliary register back on all-zero. Suppose U block-encodes A with normalizer alpha (so the auxiliary-zero projected block equals A/alpha) and the input system state is a normalized vector v. Express the unnormalized clean output branch and its squared norm, give the exact success probability of the all-zero postselection, and state when this probability equals (||A v|| / alpha)^2. Why is the success probability generally strictly below 1, and what does this cost imply for using the block encoding as a subroutine?

items.question: Suppose a non-unitary matrix A acting on n qubits is embedded as the top-left block of a larger unitary, in the sense that applying the unitary to an input with the ancilla register prepared in all-zeros, and then measuring the ancillas and keeping only the all-zeros outcome, applies A to the system state. More generally the embedded block equals A divided by a positive subnormalization factor alpha. For an input system state |b>, derive the probability of the kept (all-zeros) outcome, express it in terms of A, |b> and alpha, and explain two consequences: how the norm of A|b> can be recovered from the measured success probability, and why choosing alpha too large is harmful. Confirm the output state conditioned on success is the correctly normalized version of A|b>.

items.question: A target operator is written as a linear combination T = sum_i alpha_i U_i of unitaries U_i, and is implemented by a prepare-select-unprepare scheme in which each coefficient is split as alpha_i = beta_i gamma_i, a left preparation loads the vector of beta_i (normalized by the 2-norm of beta), a controlled selection applies U_i, and a right unpreparation loads the vector of gamma_i. The resulting construction embeds T with subnormalization factor equal to the product of the 2-norms of the beta and gamma vectors. Prove, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, that this subnormalization factor is at least the 1-norm of the coefficient vector alpha, and determine the splitting beta_i, gamma_i that makes the factor equal to that 1-norm. Explain why this is the best (smallest) achievable factor for this scheme and hence the most favorable success probability.
